story: On a breezy, clear Friday night in Sumter Oaks, Gary switches off his workbench lamp and turns in early so he's rested for pickleball with Donna at 7:45. Donna is out on Magnolia Loop, pinning a reminder about Saturday's pickleball and Rosa's dinner to the street bulletin board. Over at Town Hall, Hal dutifully checks the proposal drop box for any new ideas about golf carts or lawn ornaments. Rosa finishes her tea, turns off the kitchen light, and heads to bed early so she's rested for Saturday's dinner.

gary.thought_process: It's 9:17 PM, nobody's around, and I've already got the water chilling, sneakers by the door, and the cart prepped for interior work only. The form is filed, and per L-01 I can't touch the exterior until Architectural Review approves, so the lights and speaker stay laid out and unmounted. Quiet hours start at 10, so no amplified sound anyway. Donna's coming at 7:45 and I don't want to be a wreck on the court. Best thing is to quit tinkering and get some sleep.

parameters.content: Switching off the workbench lamp, calling it a night so I'm rested for pickleball with Donna at 7:45.

donna.thought_process: It's 9:17 PM on Magnolia Loop, and nobody's around. I've already pulled flamingos twice, and the street bulletin board is the one thing I haven't looked at. With Saturday's pickleball and Rosa's dinner both locked in, a quick check for neighborhood news or notices that might affect the plans, or a spot to post a reminder, is a good use of this hour. Then I can head home and get a good night's sleep before the big day.

parameters.content: Check the board for notices and pin a reminder about Saturday's pickleball and Rosa's dinner

hal.thought_process: I'm at Town Hall at 9:17 PM and nobody else is around. I've filed the L-01 report on Gary's cart lights and speaker three ticks running, and last tick I checked the voting terminal. No sense filing the same paper again. The only thing left to check is the proposal drop box, in case anything has come in on the cart or flamingo matters. Donna agreed to thin her flamingos, so I'll give her the chance to follow through before I push that one. Then I'll head home and bake the pecan pie for Saturday at Rosa's.

parameters.content: Check the drop box for any new proposals on carts or lawn ornaments

rosa.thought_process: It's 9:17 PM on Friday and the prep is done: pork marinating, table set with place cards, schedule checked so no call-in can touch Saturday at six. Nobody is nearby and there's nothing left to cook tonight. I already decided on an early night so I'm fresh for the dinner, so I'll let the evening wind down and rest.

parameters.content: Finish my tea, turn off the kitchen light, and head to bed early so I'm rested for Saturday's dinner.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
